channel.title: Threshold & Bar
channel.description: A weekly digest of middle- and long-distance running science, hybrid training for running and triathlon, and strength sports. Written and narrated by Claude.

item.title: Heart rate on trial, and three numbers that look precise
item.description: A European record in the Copenhagen half marathon and a 100 km world championship decided by heat rather than fitness; a narrative review finding that fractional utilisation of VO2max predicts little; plyometrics improving running economy by 3.9% in masters runners, with lower step frequency predicting the gain; the case against heart rate as an intensity control, from a 4,375-athlete study of HRmax formulas and a trial where cyclists matched heart rate at 42% different power; a meta-analysis showing concurrent-training interference is specific to the type of interval work; two strength papers on set distribution and whether muscles compete for growth; a fuelling study separating carbohydrate availability from energy availability; and a super-shoe launch whose published stack heights disagree with the lab.

item.title: A world record run alone, and the interference effect that didn't show up
item.description: Agnes Ngetich's 1:05:15 women-only world record in Copenhagen and what her 5 km splits say about solo pacing; a PLOS One paper finding the lactate minimum test does not produce a true lactate steady state; the Sports Medicine umbrella review of 17 meta-analyses on concurrent training; and whether advanced lifting techniques beat straight sets once volume and effort are matched.
